Subject: Sizing confirmation + contract term question for Redwood Dedicated

Hi Alex,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. We have two follow-ups from procurement and engineering before we can move to legal:

- Sizing: engineering confirmed the initial throughput estimate (peak 3.8k tokens/s sustained per model) and wants a 10% physical buffer. Can you confirm the SKU mix you recommended for the Dedicated pool and whether we can start with a 60/40 split (A100-80 / H100)?
- Term & pricing: procurement is concerned about GPU spot price volatility over a 36-month commit. They asked whether Redwood will accept an "index-swap" clause (allowing substitution between GPU SKUs tied to a cloud GPU cost index) or a pricing-floor with a pass-through for large market moves.

I attached the preliminary SOW for your reference. High level ask: can you propose an amendment that shows 3 scenarios (base, +25% GPU cost shock, -15% GPU cost drop) and the commercial adjustments for each? We need that to justify our internal approval.

Target timeline: procurement wants a commercial response by EOD Friday (2026-10-09).

Thanks,
Alex Gomez
Sr. Procurement Manager
Novamed
(attachment: novamed_prelim_sow.pdf)

From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>

Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-07T09:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sizing confirmation + contract term question for Redwood Dedicated

Alex —

Appreciate the clear asks. Short answers up front: yes on the 60/40 mix as a starting point (we'll stage H100 ramp over Q1 to match your latency targets), and yes — we can offer an index-swap mechanism with guardrails plus a pricing-floor option.

I've put together a compact term matrix (attached) that shows:
- Scenario A (Base): 36-month commit, fixed per-GPU unit price, 10% buffer included in billed capacity.
- Scenario B (+25% GPU cost shock): automatic swap allowance to lower-cost compatible SKUs + temporary 8% surcharge that phases out after 3 months or when market index retreats.
- Scenario C (-15% GPU cost drop): pass-through credit to customer (applied as monthly invoice credit).

Key commercial asks from our side:
1) Approval to include a capped pricing-floor (protects Redwood if costs spike beyond a pre-agreed cap).
2) Executive sign-off for discount exceptions if Novamed requires deeper initial discounts to hit procurement thresholds (we're proposing an internal approval threshold at 20% typical; anything >20% needs VP review).

I've attached rdw_term_matrix_v1.xlsx and a CSV with sensitivity scenarios. Can Kimberly and Sean confirm internal approval path and whether we should route this through finance escalation or exec waiver? I'll consolidate and send a clean proposal to you by EOD Friday.

Best,
Alex Martinez
Enterprise Sales (Dedicated)
Redwood Inference
(attachments: rdw_term_matrix_v1.xlsx, sensitivity_scenarios.csv)

Subject: Re: Dedicated GPU pool — index-swap & tier matrix (internal)

Alex / Sean —

Reviewed the term matrix. A few notes from finance/commercial controls:

- Pricing-floor: finance is okay with a floor tied to a 3-month trailing GPU index, but we need a cap on our exposure. Propose we set the floor so that Redwood retains at least a 12% gross margin at base utilization assumptions.
- Index-swap: acceptable if swaps are limited to certified SKU families (A100/H100 family and one medium-performance fall-back). Swaps should not reduce throughput below the agreed SLA.
- Discount approval: my team authorizes up to a 18% list discount on Reserved pricing for strategic plays. Anything >18% requires COO or VP Sales sign-off and must include a documented ramp plan (usage milestones).

Operational asks: add a clause that gives Redwood the right to perform a quarterly capacity rebalancing if sustained utilization deviates >15% from forecast; that protects us from overcommit.

I'll pre-clear the approach with Laura (finance) for an exec waiver if Alex/Gomez press for deeper concessions. If you want, I can draft the redline for legal with the floor/index language.

Kimberly
Director, Commercial Finance
Redwood Inference
